source.title: A Quadrature Perspective on Frequency Bias in Neural Network Training with Nonuniform Data
source.authors: Annan Yu; Yu-Nan Yang; Alex Townsend

record.tranche_reason: The paper mentions double descent as background motivation and cites prior work, but its own analysis and experiments concern frequency-component learning, not test-risk curves over model size, epochs, or sample size.
record.gate_note: The reported frequency-loss and denoising outcomes are related to training dynamics but do not measure double-descent test error. The double-descent mention is introductory only.
record.test_reason: Double descent appears only as introductory motivation (citing Belkin et al., 2019). The paper's theory and experiments concern frequency biasing in NTK-regime 2-layer ReLU training with nonuniform data and Sobolev losses. No test-error curve over model size, epochs or sample count is reported, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that frequency biasing holds for 2-layer ReLU NTK training with nonuniform data, up to quadrature errors. They add that a Sobolev H^s loss can amplify, dampen, counterbalance or reverse it, and that this helps denoising in an MNIST autoencoder. They draw no conclusion about double descent.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes and experiments on frequency-component learning with nonuniform data and Sobolev losses, rather than testing the original double-descent risk-curve method.
record.method_sensitivity: Frequency-component learning changes with the loss choice and Sobolev parameter s; the text reports low-frequency bias for s = -1 and s = 0, and reversal for s = 2.5 on S2 and s = 3 on S1.

fits_no_version.finding: With nonuniform data, quadrature-weighted L2 loss makes low-frequency-first learning more evident than standard MSE, where it is not guaranteed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Frequency (spectral) bias in overparameterized NN training persists for nonuniform data when the loss uses data-dependent quadrature weights.

fits_no_version.finding: A squared Sobolev H^s loss tunes frequency bias: s<0 enhances low-frequency bias, while large s (s>2 on S1, s=2.5 on S2) reverses it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sobolev-norm loss weighting can amplify or reverse the spectral bias of NN training.

record.problems: The experiments address frequency-component loss rather than test error or double descent. Most outcomes are shown in plots without numerical values in the text. The synthetic demonstrations use two-layer ReLU networks on spheres; the MNIST denoising experiment does not assess double-descent risk.
record.rows_left_out: The MNIST autoencoder denoising illustrations in Section 6.3 and Figure 4 are not included: they report qualitative image outputs for deliberately added frequency-specific noise, not a result on the double-descent claim or a frequency-loss measure.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep or test error; network width is fixed (5×10^4 neurons).
Per-frequency training-fit losses over epochs are reported, not test error over epochs.
No variation of training sample count against test error.
No risk curves across capacity or model classes.
No effective-complexity measure or peak location.
Noise appears only as added image noise in the MNIST denoising demo; no double-descent peak or regularization sweep.

record.verdict_notes: The record's rows are correctly linked to none; the cannot_determine states are acceptable because values are figure-only. Rows r1–r6 measure training-fit frequency components on the training function, not generalization risk. The MNIST omission is properly declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Model-size sweep and test error near the interpolation threshold.
Test error over epochs; frequency-component fitting is not test error.
Effect of increasing training sample count near an interpolation threshold on test error.
Risk curves across model classes as capacity passes the interpolation point.
A shared effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations.
Whether noise or regularization drives double-descent peaks, including multiple peaks or their disappearance under optimal regularization.
Whether effective parameter counting turns second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.value: The text says frequency biasing is not guaranteed with Φ and is not always observed in this experiment; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: Reports frequency-component fitting, not test error or a double-descent curve.

rows.note: This is a comparison of frequency learning, not test error.
